source.title: Fast Unlearning at Scale via Margin Self-Correction
source.authors: F. Di Gennaro; A. Shevchenko; Fanny Yang

record.tranche_reason: The study tests how post-unlearning 4-bit quantization changes forget-set memorization, and evaluates memorization under paraphrased questions. These are direct tests of recovery claims using the study's methods and models.
record.gate_note: The 4-bit quantization results in Table 3 compare quantized unlearned checkpoints with their full-precision counterparts; Table 2 supplies the full-precision values. The scaling study evaluates unlearned models with paraphrased Q&A prompts, but the plotted values in Figure 4 are not stated numerically. No relearning attack or activation-direction ablation is run. Other methods' results cited in the introduction and related work are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: A new unlearning method paper, MASC, that includes its own 4-bit quantization attack (Appendix D.1, Table 3). The attack is run on MASC and six baselines on MUSE News and Books, measuring forget-set memorization before and after quantization. These are direct results on D (quantization recovery) and on F (MASC's robustness claim). Full-precision Tables 1–2 bear on A. The paraphrased Q&A scaling results bear on E only as figures.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The main conclusion is that MASC's self-stopping margin objective achieves a competitive forget–retain trade-off at a fraction of the baselines' runtime. They also report that MASC stays low on forget metrics after 4-bit quantization while several baselines rise. After unlearning, forget metrics are roughly scale-invariant while retain utility improves with size. They say MASC appears to improve paraphrase-level forgetting, though their bound does not control it.
record.recipe_differences: MASC is a margin-based unlearning method with an online stopping rule; the study does not reproduce the original recovery attacks generally, but specifically applies 4-bit quantization and paraphrased-prompt evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Quantization effects vary by method, dataset, and metric. The Qwen2.5 scaling study reports forget-side metrics in a similar range across model sizes after unlearning.
record.problems: No chance-level reference is stated for the forget metrics. Quantization outcomes are reported without uncertainty in Table 3. Paraphrased-prompt results in Figure 4 are not stated numerically. The attack evaluation covers 4-bit quantization and paraphrased Q&A, not the other attack types in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were left out. Base and retrain quantization rows in Table 3 were omitted because they are not unlearned checkpoints; cited attack results from other studies were also omitted.

untested.parts: No activation ablation or access-vs-deletion analysis.
Only 4-bit tested; no 8-bit or other quantization schemes.
No jailbreaks, other languages or in-context attacks. Paraphrase values are given in figures only.
MASC is not tested against relearning, activation edits, prompting attacks or other bit widths.
Simple attacks other than 4-bit quantization are not tested. There is no WMDP/MMLU-style general-capability check.

missing.what: Base 4-bit and Retrain 4-bit forget metrics. These show that quantization alone lowers memorization in base models, which is needed to interpret D.
Unlearning-stage scaling fits for E-ROUGE vs P-ROUGE (fitted C 0.39 vs 0.31 for MASC), giving approximate paraphrase levels.

record.verdict_notes: The record's version codes (V1, V4, V5) were remapped to A, D and E/F. Retrain values in Tables 2–3 serve as the chance-equivalent reference. GA and NPO collapse to zero retain utility on MUSE, so their quantization outcomes say little about hidden knowledge. Zhang et al. (quantization attack) is cited and is not among this phenomenon's original sources.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish a chance-level reference for its forget metrics. Its attack evaluation is limited to 4-bit quantization; it does not test other attacks.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set is used to test recovery.
No activation-direction ablation or access-blocking analysis is tested.
Only 4-bit quantization is evaluated; other bit widths and quantization schemes are not stated.
Paraphrased Q&A evaluation is included in the Qwen2.5 scaling study. Jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
MASC is evaluated against 4-bit quantization, but not against fine-tuning, activation edits, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.

source_check.notes: Table 2 lost its layout. The News block (base 57.25/66.45/54.90) is Llama-2 7B and the Books block (99.70/47.12/69.13) is ICLM-7B: 'Method / Base (Llama-2 7B)' heads the first block as in Table 1, and these are MUSE's target models. The record swaps the models on all MUSE rows and mixes News and Books baselines (R7-R10, notes on R8/R18/R30/R33/R37). Code is released (footnote 3), though the pack says code: n. The quantization scheme is not stated, and Table 3 has no std.

statements.correction: MUSE Books (ICLM-7B), MASC KnowMem Dfg 47.12->30.90 (retrain 30.29); retain KnowMem 69.13->65.30. MUSE News (Llama-2 7B): 66.45->19.37 (retrain 32.55).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MASC on MUSE News and MUSE Books; TOFU retain utility
reader_labels.reason: MASC substantially reduces forget metrics and retains some utility, but nonzero forget scores remain, MUSE News retained knowledge is much lower than base, and the study supplies no chance-level reference; see R4–R10.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: 4-bit quantization of unlearned models with increased forget metrics
reader_labels.reason: Several methods show increases after quantization, but the increases are mixed in size and do not consistently restore the full-precision-to-base gap; see R17–R22, R25–R26, R30–R34, and R38.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Methods and dataset metrics with no increase or reduced memorization after 4-bit quantization
reader_labels.reason: Quantization leaves some forget metrics unchanged and lowers others, including both reported MASC metrics on MUSE Books; see R13–R16, R23–R24, R27–R29, R35–R37.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Paraphrased Q&A evaluation after MASC and SimNPO on TOFU across Qwen2.5 sizes
reader_labels.reason: The study evaluates paraphrased prompts after unlearning, but the reported figure values are not numerically stated, so recovery under rephrasing cannot be determined; see R39–R46.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MASC on MUSE Books under 4-bit quantization
reader_labels.reason: Both MASC forget metrics decrease slightly rather than increase after quantization; see R13–R14.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MASC on MUSE News under 4-bit quantization
reader_labels.reason: MASC's forget metrics increase under quantization on MUSE News, though the study describes the resulting forget-set memorization as low; see R11–R12.
